question: Which Article defines State and Union Territories for the purposes of the Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 1 of the Indian Constitution defines India as a "Union of States."
 
• It specifies that India shall be divided into states and union territories for administrative purposes.
 
• Article 1 establishes the territorial composition of India, including states, union territories, and any other territories that may be acquired.
 
• The inclusion of terms like "Union of States" emphasizes the indestructible nature of the Indian Union.
 
• This Article is crucial for understanding the territorial framework of the nation as per constitutional provisions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 3:**

 
 
• Article 3 deals with the formation of new states and alteration of existing states' boundaries or names.
 
• It empowers Parliament to make laws for creating new states, merging states, or altering boundaries or names of states.
 
• Before introducing such a bill, the President must refer it to the concerned state's legislature for their opinion, although their opinion is not binding.
 
 
 
• **Article 239:**
 
 
• Article 239 pertains to the administration of Union Territories.
 
• It states that every Union Territory shall be administered by the President through an administrator appointed by him.
 
• This Article establishes the framework for governance in regions not classified as states under the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Article 240:**
 
 
• Article 240 grants the President the authority to make regulations for Union Territories that do not have legislatures.
 
• This power can be exercised in territories like Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu, and Puducherry under special circumstances.
 
• The regulations made by the President under this Article have the same force as laws passed by Parliament.
